lede: The big one this week is Wednesday's joint Planning Commission and BOCC work session, where San Miguel County works through proposed Land Use Code amendments covering forestry practices, oil and gas operations, deep geothermal, and condominium plats — the kind of code-shaping session that quietly sets the rules for years of development decisions to come. Also Wednesday, the BOCC heads to Norwood for a rare West End meeting to consider a Planning Commission appointment and hear results from the Placerville Fire Survey — two items worth tracking if you care about land use and fire preparedness in the broader valley.

notable.stake: County land use code amendments on forestry, oil, gas, geothermal, and condos being shaped.
Commissioners may appoint a Planning Commission alternate; fire survey results presented publicly.
